files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: P. Guerrero. Complete in sequence; no skipping ahead.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July; some months all runs pay in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and contracts. Check the GL first to prevent duplication. If it has not been posted, book June prepaid amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL to ensure it has not already been recorded.
5. Verify the expense coding on June vendor bills by comparing the bill documents with the GL. Reclass anything miscoded to the correct expense account.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, only after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Harborview Consulting LLP began in 2018 when two former in-house operators realized that many growing organizations needed experienced help without another permanent layer of management. They set up a compact advisory practice built around plain language, practical recommendations, and a willingness to stay through implementation rather than leave clients with a presentation deck.

The firm sells project-based strategy, operations, process improvement, and management advisory services. Engagements often start with interviews and workflow reviews, then move into facilitated planning, decision support, and hands-on coordination with client teams. Harborview’s clients span established local businesses, health organizations, consumer brands, and industrial companies.

The team has a distinctly working-session culture. Partners lead engagements directly, consultants trade templates freely, and the office is known for marked-up whiteboards, strong coffee, and concise internal notes. Specialists in legal, accounting, marketing, and technology are brought in when a project calls for expertise outside the core team.

Currently, Harborview Consulting LLP is balancing active client delivery with the routine work of sharpening its market position and improving internal systems. Leadership is refining service packages, documenting repeatable methods, and developing a steadier referral pipeline while preserving the responsive, senior-led approach that clients value.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Position Harborview Consulting LLP as the practical advisory firm for teams that need senior attention and usable answers, not extra ceremony. Keep the tone confident, specific, and human.

## Priorities

- Refresh the brand story around hands-on strategy, operations, and implementation.
- Publish short field notes drawn from recurring client challenges, with identifying details removed.
- Host two focused webinars per quarter, each built around a real operating question rather than a broad trend.
- Test a partner co-marketing pilot with complementary legal, accounting, and technology firms.
- Give partners a simple follow-up kit for referrals, event attendees, and dormant relationships.

## Campaign themes

For Q3, emphasize clearing operational bottlenecks and turning plans into accountable work. For Q4, shift toward planning discipline, management cadence, and readiness for the next operating cycle.

## Channels

Use the firm website as the source of record, then adapt material for email, professional social channels, partner newsletters, and webinar follow-up. Favor useful checklists, brief case examples, and direct partner commentary over generic thought leadership.

## Measurement

Track qualified conversations, referral activity, webinar engagement, content reuse, and movement from first contact to scoped discussion. Review results at each quarter close and retain only the tactics that produce credible client interest.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from your predecessor

P. Guerrero — a few things that will save you some hunting at close:

- The bank’s own service fees and charges usually appear near the end of the statement. We have historically picked them up and booked them during the close.
- Do not assume the June vendor-bill coding is clean. A couple of bills may be sitting in the wrong expense account; when the GL and support disagree, the documents in `bills/` are authoritative.
- The Q2 budget was locked in early April. The one-off items that arrived in June were never included in the plan, so they are the main explanation for the large variances.
- Payroll timing is different this time: the second June run pays in early July. Check the payroll register and handle the cutoff accordingly.
